bullets.title: MU: Bullish setup into earnings tonight; DRAM +21% Q/Q, supply tight through 2H27
bullets.body: KeyBanc (OW, $1,750 PT) reports September DRAM pricing +21.3% Q/Q / +0.9% M/M and NAND +3.2% Q/Q; HBM supply-constrained with CY27 expected tighter than CY26. MS desk expects MU August Q EPS ~$33 vs cons $31.49 and Nov Q guide $37-38 vs cons $35.07. UBS's Arcuri raises CY27/28/29 EPS to $212/$277/$219, maintaining $1,625 PT; server DDR demand +80% YoY, SSD bit demand >100% YoY with DRAM fulfillment still ~60%.

bullets.title: JBL: FY27 guidance raised to $44.5B rev / $17.55 EPS on 54% AI growth; margins the watch item
bullets.body: Jabil Q4 beat ($10.6B rev, $4.40 EPS vs JPMe $4.15) and raised FY27 guidance: revenue $44.5B (+24% YoY), core EPS $17.55 (+34%), AI revenue ~$22.1B (+54%). JPM (OW) flags soft gross margins (9.4% vs 9.7% expected) and FY27 FCF of only $1.6B implying <90% FCF/NI conversion vs 100%+ historical as key investor concerns. A second hyperscaler is expected to become a 10%+ customer in FY27.

bullets.title: NVDA: CEO/CFO bullish NDR in NYC today; OpenAI CPT6.1 Sol runs on NVDA chips, not Cerebras
bullets.body: NVDA hosts Jensen Huang and CFO in NYC today with bullish IR deck showing Feynman reaching ~$60B per GW and open model token growth +25x YoY. OpenAI's CPT6.1 Sol Ultrafast confirmed running on NVDA GPUs (not CBRS), sending NVDA +0.9% pre-market and CBRS -4.6%. MS desk views hyperscalers poised to outperform into earnings with compute demand visibility through 2027.

bullets.title: MDB: Raises long-term growth targets to 20%+; CEO departure creates show-me overhang
bullets.body: MongoDB Investor Day raised medium-term revenue growth to 20%+ (from high-teens) and Atlas growth to mid-20s%; AI-native revenue ~$100M+ ARR growing +165% YoY. CEO CJ Desai departed for META; new management emphasizes continuity. DA Davidson reiterates Buy at $415 PT (36x EV/FY28 FCF vs 45x for comparable peers); Piper and Citi also reiterate Buy, noting Rule of 45-50 in ~3 years.

bullets.title: HPE: Raises FY27 networking growth to +17-20% on $1.2B Vultr Helios win; re-rating candidate
bullets.body: HPE raised FY27 networking segment growth outlook by 3-4pts to +17-20% YoY following a $1.2B Helios rack order from Vultr — the first such order and first guidance raise in a month. Record AI orders stand at $3.1B with $7.6B backlog. MS desk notes HPE trades at low-teens P/E vs DELL high-teens and has networking upside DELL lacks; FY27 EPS framework $4.35-$4.62 appears below Street at $4.75+.

bullets.title: META: Muse holds #1 App Store spot; OpenAI DevDay a net relief for META bulls
bullets.body: META Muse personal AI agent holds #1 App Store position while OpenAI Dots launched limited to paid Pro tier only ($200/month), signaling compute constraints and narrower consumer reach. Citi notes META rallied ~3% during/after DevDay; no cyber content in Dots reduces competitive threat. MS and KeyBanc flag META consumer focus offers clearer near-term growth than GOOGL facing innovator's dilemma.

bullets.title: OpenAI DevDay: Dots agent + GPT-6.1 Sol bullish for NET/AKAM infra; bearish read for CRM/HUBS
bullets.body: OpenAI ARR surged 70% in Q3 to ~$70B; B2B revenue doubled since July. Dots is a cloud-based agent running continuously across 4,000+ apps; GPT-6.1 Sol matches Astra capability at 1/5 the token cost. RBC sees bullish impact for NET and AKAM on agent traffic surge; bearish disruption narrative for HUBS and CRM. KeyBanc argues consensus is underestimating 2027/2028 hyperscaler capex for AMZN, GOOGL, and META.

bullets.title: TLN: New CEO named; $1.5B accelerated buyback funded by PJM capacity monetization
bullets.body: TLN president Terry Nutt named CEO effective Jan 1, replacing retiring Mac McFarland. Company announces $1.5B accelerated share repurchase and upsizes total buyback to $3B, funded via monetization of PJM 2027-29 cleared capacity revenues; forecasts ~$4B adjusted FCF from H2'26 through end '28. FERC's 5-month PJM Reliability Backstop suspension is slightly negative for TLN/CEG/VST but path remains intact and supports power price rally.

bullets.title: TSLA: Q3 delivery estimate 441K, -11% YoY; energy margin below historical 30%+
bullets.body: MS and multiple desks estimate TSLA Q3 deliveries at 441K (vs consensus 462K), down 11% YoY and 8% QoQ on softer US demand and China domestic sales. Energy storage expected at 16.3 GWh (+30% YoY) but energy business gross margin guided ~26.5%, below historical 30%+ due to pricing pressure and tariff headwinds.

bullets.title: MSFT: Piper raises PT to $610 on Copilot/M365 consumption path; technically stalled below Aug highs
bullets.body: Piper raises MSFT PT to $610, citing M365 consumption revenue path to $2B run rate by FY28; every 10% shift of E5 to E7 seats drives ~$2B annualized revenue uplift. JPM technical chartbook notes MSFT stalled below August highs with support at 477-486 and critical support at 465-466. Hedgeye is buying XLK (MSFT+AAPL ~40% of ETF) on weakness as preferred large-cap tech expression.

bullets.title: TTD: Apple iOS 27 Safari ad-blocking issue flagged as low-single-digit revenue headwind
bullets.body: KeyBanc flags that Trade Desk ads are being blocked on Safari for iOS 27 devices; issue was surfaced by TTD on Sept 21 with no resolution as of Sept 28. Analyst views the block as a potentially low-single-digit percentage headwind to annual revenue if it persists; KeyBanc maintains sector weight.

bullets.title: DKNG: Weakness tied to Kalshi $1B fundraise and CFTC crackdown fears; at 52-week low
bullets.body: Citi attributes DKNG weakness to Kalshi's $1B fundraise, fears of CFTC crackdown on prediction market promotions, and uncertainty ahead of G2E conference. DKNG is now down 54.2% from its 52-week high per the 52-week high/low screen.

bullets.title: APP: Down 57.9% from 52-week high; -1.4% pre-market post-earnings
bullets.body: APP appeared on both the 52-week low screen (down 57.9% from peak) and the pre-market movers list (-1.4% post-earnings). No specific analyst commentary on earnings details in this window.

bullets.title: SHOP: Nationwide money transmitter licenses could add 2% GP / 5% EBIT by 2028
bullets.body: Zach AM Attack highlights SHOP's expanding payment economics via nationwide money transmitter licenses as a key upside driver, potentially adding 2% gross profit and 5% EBIT uplift by 2028. Piper is separately constructive on W (Wayfair) accelerating share gains. SHOP trading +1.5% in Canadian pre-market.

bullets.title: AAPL: Soft iPhone 18 resale premiums signal weak demand; smart home hub launch Oct 13
bullets.body: Weak Pro/Pro Max resale premiums flagged as a leading indicator of softer iPhone 18 demand. AAPL to unveil a 6" smart home hub and HomePod mini refresh on Oct 13, with CEO overhaul focused on faster product release cycles. Hedgeye prefers XLK exposure (MSFT+AAPL ~40%) over direct AAPL long.

bullets.title: Bernstein initiates ANET OW at $250, CIEN OW at $440, CLS OW at $520, COHR OW at $350; CSCO/GLW market perform
bullets.body: Bernstein initiates coverage on five communications equipment names: Arista (ANET) outperform $250, Ciena (CIEN) outperform $440, Celestica (CLS) outperform $520, Coherent (COHR) outperform $350, and Cisco (CSCO) market perform $110, Corning (GLW) market perform $140.

bullets.title: CCL: MS raises PT to $32.50 on clean Q3 beat; short crowding at highs per Citi quant
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raises CCL FY26/27 EPS to $2.28/$2.56 and PT to $32.50 (from $31) after a clean Q3 beat with stronger yields, lower costs, and accelerating bookings/onboard spending (+7.7% vs +5.2% in Q2). FY26-29 EPS CAGR implied at 17%. Separately, Citi quant notes CCL short crowding is steadily increasing and at highs, providing a contrarian setup.

bullets.title: META/GOOGL: FTC opens investigation into frontier AI labs; CIDs expected in coming weeks
bullets.body: FTC launched an investigation into major AI labs including Google and Meta a few weeks ago, reportedly prior to a Hugging Face incident. Civil investigative demands (CIDs) for documents and key leader testimony are expected to go out imminently, focused on alleged unfair/deceptive trade practices or FTC Act violations.

bullets.title: WBD/PSKY: Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz joins Paramount Skydance Warner Bros. Discovery in senior role
bullets.body: Ynon Kreiz steps down as Mattel CEO effective Oct 2 to join Paramount Skydance Warner Bros. Discovery in a senior leadership role. Roger Lynch (current board member) takes over as MAT Chairman immediately and CEO on or before Nov 2. UBS maintains Buy on MAT at $28 PT, calling the transition relatively smooth with the IP monetization thesis intact.

bullets.title: CRWV/NBIS: William Blair initiates both at Outperform; JPM hosting joint equity/credit call on CRWV
bullets.body: William Blair initiates CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) both at Outperform; CRWV +2.2% and NBIS +3.0% in pre-market. JPM is separately hosting a joint equity and credit discussion on CoreWeave to address business fundamentals and capital structure implications.
